source_text: Διὰ τοῦτο οὐ μόνον ἐξ ἀγρῶν καὶ προσόδων, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐκ τῆς τῶν χειρῶν ἐργασίας μεταδιδόναι τοῖς μὴ ἔχουσιν ὁ Ἀπόστολος παραινεῖ· Ἐργαζόμενοι φησὶ, τὸ ἀγαθὸν ταῖς χερσὶν, ἵνα ἔχητε μεταδιδόναι τῷ χρείαν ἔχοντι. Τῷ δὲ ἀκολουθεῖν βουλομένῳ, καὶ πᾶσαν πιπράσκειν τὴν οὐσίαν εἰς εὐεργεσίαν πενήτων ὁ Κύριος εἰσηγήσατο, καὶ οὕτως ἀκολουθεῖν αὐτῷ· τοῖς μὲν ἀκολουθηταῖς καὶ τελείοις τὴν ἀθρόον καὶ τελείαν τῶν ἐλεημοσυνῶν πλήρωσιν ἐπιτάττων, ἵνα, πληρώσαντες τὴν διὰ χρημάτων λειτουργίαν, ἐπὶ τὴν διὰ λόγου καὶ πνεύματος μεταβῶσι· τοῖς δὲ λοιποῖς τὰς, ἐξ ὧν ἔχουσι, μεταδόσεις καὶ κοινωνίας διηνεκεῖς παραγγέλλων, ἵνα διὰ τούτων εὑρεθῶσι Θεοῦ φιλανθρωπίας μιμηταὶ, ἐλεοῦντές τε καὶ μεταδιδόντες καὶ χαριζόμενοι. Δίδοτε γὰρ, φησὶ, καὶ δοθήσεται ὑμῖν. Διὰ τούτων δὲ καὶ τὴν πρὸς ἑαυτὸν κοινωνίαν ἑαυτοῖς ἐπηγγείλατο. Οὗτοι γάρ εἰσιν οἱ ἐκ δεξιῶν ἱστάμενοι τοῦ Κυρίου, πρὸς οὓς ἐρεῖ παραγενόμενος ὁ βασιλεύς· Δεῦτε, οἱ εὐλογημένοι τοῦ Πατρός μου, κληρονομήσατε τὴν ἡτοιμασμένην ὑμῖν βασιλείαν ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου. Ἐπείνασα γὰρ, καὶ ἐδώκατέ μοι φαγεῖν· ἐδίψησα, καὶ ἐποτίσατέ με· γυμνὸς ἤμην, καὶ περιεβάλετέ με· ξένος, καὶ συνηγάγετέ με· ἀσθενὴς καὶ ἐν φυλακῇ, καὶ ἤλθετε πρὸς μέ. Θαυμασάντων δὲ τῶν δικαίων καὶ εἰπόντων· Πότε ταῦτα ἐποιήσαμεν εἰς σὲ, Κύριε; ἐρεῖ πρὸς αὐτούς· Ἀμὴν, ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐφ' ὅσον ἐποιήσατε ἑνὶ τούτων τῶν ἀδελφῶν μου τῶν ἐλαχίστων, ἐμοὶ ἐποιήσατε. Ἡ γὰρ εἰς τοὺς ἁγίους προθυμία εἰς Χριστόν ἐστιν εὐσέβεια, καὶ ὁ πρὸς τὸν πτωχὸν πρόθυμος ὑπηρέτης εὑρίσκεται Χριστοῦ κοινωνός· οὐ μόνον, εἰ μεταδοίη τι μέγα ἔχων, ἀλλ' εἰ καὶ μικρὸν κεκτημένος, τοῦτο προσάγοι, καὶ εἰ ποτήριον ψυχρὸν μόνον ποτίσειε τὸν μαθητὴν εἰς ὄνομα μαθητοῦ. Ἡ γὰρ τῶν μαθητῶν ἔνδεια κατὰ τὸν κόσμον ἀληθινοῦ σοι πλούτου πρόφασις, ὦ πλούσιε. Διὰ γὰρ τούτων εὑρίσκῃ Χριστοῦ συνεργός· στρατιώτας τρέφεις Χριστοῦ, καὶ τρέφεις ἑκὼν, οὐκ ἀναγκαζόμενος. Ὁ γὰρ οὐράνιος βασιλεὺς οὐκ ἐπαναγκάζει, οὐδὲ ἀπαιτεῖ τελέσματα, ἀλλὰ δέχεται τοὺς προθυμουμένους, ἵνα διδόντες λάβωσι, καὶ τιμήσαντες τιμηθῶσι, καὶ κοινωνήσαντες τῶν προσκαίρων, εἰς κοινωνίαν τῶν αἰωνίων κληθῶσι. Ταῦτα ἡμῖν ἐν παντὶ καιρῷ διὰ μνήμης ἔστω, καὶ πρὸ ὀφθαλμῶν τῆς ψυχῆς, ἵνα μὴ παραλίπωμεν τὸν ἐμπεσόντα καιρὸν, μηδὲ ὑπερθέμενοι τὸν παρ-όντα, ἕτερον ἀναμείνωμεν, μήποτε ἐν τῷ μένειν καὶ ἀναβάλλεσθαι τῷ τέλει καταληφθῶμεν. Δῴη δὲ ὁ Κύριος ἐγκάρπους ἡμᾶς καὶ γρηγοροῦντας καὶ τῶν ἐντολῶν αὐτοῦ μεμνημένους εἰς τὴν ἀπάντησιν αὐτοῦ τὴν ἔνδοξον ἑτοίμους καὶ ἀνεμποδίστους εὑρεθῆναι, ἐν αὐτῷ τῷ Χριστῷ καὶ Θεῷ ἡμῶν, μεθ' οὗ τῷ Πατρὶ καὶ τῷ ἁγίῳ Πνεύματι δόξα, κράτος, τιμὴ, νῦν καὶ ἀεὶ, καὶ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. Ἀμήν.
thought_title: Mercy to the poor is service to Christ and will be rewarded
orientation: Basil is concluding his homily by showing that almsgiving and sharing with the poor are service to Christ himself, who will reward them at the judgment.
pass_a_gloss: For this reason the Apostle urges not only from fields and revenues but also from the work of the hands to share with those who do not have. Working, he says, the good with the hands, in order that you may have to share with the one who has need. And to the one wishing to follow, and to sell all his property for the benefit of the poor, the Lord gave instruction, and thus to follow him. To the followers and perfect ones he commands the complete and perfect fulfillment of almsgivings, in order that, having fulfilled the service through money, they may pass over to the service through word and spirit. And to the rest he commands the distributions and continual sharings from what they have, in order that through these they may be found imitators of God's kindness, showing mercy and sharing and giving freely. For give, he says, and it will be given to you. And through these he promised to them also the sharing with himself. For these are the ones standing at the right of the Lord, to whom the king will say when he comes: Come, you who are blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world. For I hungered, and you gave me to eat; I thirsted, and you gave me drink; I was naked, and you clothed me; a stranger, and you gathered me in; weak and in prison, and you came to me. And when the righteous marvel and say: When did we do these things to you, Lord? he will say to them: Amen, amen I say to you, inasmuch as you did it to one of these my brothers, the least, you did it to me. For the eagerness toward the saints is piety toward Christ, and the eager servant toward the poor is found a sharer of Christ; not only if he should share something great while having much, but even if having little, he should offer this, and even if he should give drink only a cup of cold water to the disciple in the name of a disciple. For the need of the disciples according to the world is an occasion of true wealth for you, O rich man. For through these you are found a fellow worker of Christ; you feed soldiers of Christ, and you feed willingly, not being compelled. For the heavenly king does not compel, nor does he demand taxes, but he receives those who are eager, in order that giving they may receive, and honoring they may be honored, and sharing in the temporary things, they may be called into the sharing of the eternal things. Let these things be to us in every season through remembrance, and before the eyes of the soul, in order that we may not let pass the season that has fallen upon us, nor, putting off the present one, wait for another, lest while waiting and delaying we be overtaken by the end. And may the Lord grant us to be found fruitful and watchful and remembering his commandments, ready and unhindered for his glorious meeting, in Christ himself our God, with whom to the Father and to the Holy Spirit be glory, might, honor, now and always, and to the ages of ages. Amen.

choices.why: The glossary reserves 'sharing' for κοινωνία, but μεταδίδωμι is the verb of giving a portion; 'to share' keeps the distributive sense and matches the brief's emphasis on sharing goods.
The glossary mandates 'almsgiving' for ἐλεημοσύνη; the plural is kept as 'almsgivings' to preserve the source's plural form.
The glossary mandates 'kindness' for φιλανθρωπία and bans 'philanthropy' and 'love for others'.
The glossary mandates 'sharing' for κοινωνία, including sharing in Christ and sharing of goods.
The term denotes eager willingness; 'eagerness' captures the voluntary, zealous disposition Basil emphasizes against compulsion.
The verb means to force or compel; keeping 'compel' preserves the contrast with the willing service Basil stresses.

pass_b_english: For this reason the Apostle urges us to share with those who have nothing not only from fields and revenues but also from the work of our hands. “Working,” he says, “the good with your hands, so that you may have something to share with the one in need” (Ephesians 4:28). To the one who wishes to follow him, the Lord also directed that he sell all his possessions for the benefit of the poor, and in this way follow him. For his followers and the perfect he commands the complete and immediate fulfillment of almsgivings, so that after completing the service that comes through money they may move on to the service that comes through word and spirit. For the rest he commands continual sharing and giving from what they have, so that through these things they may be found imitators of God’s kindness, showing mercy, sharing, and giving freely. “Give,” he says, “and it will be given to you” (Luke 6:38). Through these things he also promised them sharing with himself. These are the ones who stand at the Lord’s right hand, to whom the king will say when he comes: “Come, you who are blessed by my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world. For I was hungry, and you gave me food; I was thirsty, and you gave me drink; I was naked, and you clothed me; I was a stranger, and you welcomed me; I was sick and in prison, and you came to me” (Matthew 25:34-36). When the righteous marvel and say, “When did we do these things for you, Lord?” he will say to them: “Amen, amen, I say to you, as much as you did it to one of the least of these my brothers, you did it to me” (Matthew 25:40). For eagerness toward the saints is reverence toward Christ, and the eager servant of the poor is found to be a sharer with Christ—not only if he shares something great because he has much, but even if he possesses little and brings that, and even if he gives only a cup of cold water to a disciple in the name of a disciple (Matthew 10:42). For the disciples’ poverty in the world is an occasion for true wealth for you, O rich man. Through these you are found a fellow worker with Christ. You feed Christ’s soldiers, and you feed them willingly, not under compulsion. For the heavenly king does not compel, nor does he demand tribute, but he receives those who are eager, so that by giving they may receive, by honoring they may be honored, and by sharing in temporary things they may be called to share in eternal things. Let these things be in our memory at every moment and before the eyes of our soul, so that we do not let the opportunity that falls to us pass by, nor put off the present and wait for another, lest while we wait and delay we be overtaken by the end. May the Lord grant that we be found fruitful and watchful, remembering his commandments, ready and unhindered for his glorious meeting, in Christ himself our God, with whom to the Father and the Holy Spirit be glory, power, and honor, now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.

last_rejected.why: Source says 'working what is good with your hands'; English 'the good' as a noun is unclear and loses the moral sense.
last_rejected.fix: what is good with your hands
last_rejected.ruling: 'The good' is standard English for 'what is good'; moral sense intact. No meaning lost.

last_rejected.quote: the complete and immediate fulfillment of almsgivings
last_rejected.source_quote: τὴν ἀθρόον καὶ τελείαν τῶν ἐλεημοσυνῶν πλήρωσιν
last_rejected.why: ἀθρόον means 'all at once, wholesale, total' (sudden/lump-sum), not 'immediate' in temporal sense; 'complete and total' or 'wholesale' is meant
last_rejected.fix: the total and complete fulfillment of almsgivings
last_rejected.ruling: ἀθρόον can mean 'at once/immediate'; rendering within normal range, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.why: ἑαυτὸν refers to Christ/the Lord (masculine), not 'himself' as neuter; 'sharing with him' or 'fellowship with himself'
last_rejected.ruling: ἑαυτὸν is masculine reflexive; 'himself' correctly renders it. No ambiguity or error.

last_rejected.why: εὐσέβεια means 'piety, godliness, devotion' not 'reverence'; 'piety toward Christ' or 'devotion to Christ'
last_rejected.ruling: εὐσέβεια includes 'reverence' within its semantic range; not a meaning change.

last_rejected.why: συνεργός means 'co-worker, fellow worker' but the genitive Χριστοῦ means 'of Christ' or 'with Christ'; 'Christ's fellow worker' or 'co-worker with Christ'—but 'fellow worker with Christ' is awkward
last_rejected.ruling: 'fellow worker with Christ' correctly renders συνεργός + genitive Χριστοῦ; claim is mere preference.

last_rejected.quote: does not compel, nor does he demand tribute
last_rejected.why: τελέσματα means 'payments, dues, taxes' but in context of voluntary giving, 'demands payments' or 'exacts dues' not 'tribute' which implies state tax
last_rejected.fix: does not compel, nor does he demand payment
last_rejected.ruling: τελέσματα means 'payments/tribute'; 'tribute' is within normal range, not misleading.

last_rejected.why: ἐγκάρπος means 'fruitful, bearing fruit' but in context of spiritual readiness, 'fruit-bearing' or 'productive'; however, 'fruitful' is within range
last_rejected.ruling: ἐγκάρπους means 'fruitful'; translation is accurate. Claim itself admits it is within range.
